text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: This paper presents a GIS-based land use model—the LAND USE SCANNER—applied at the national scale (the entire Netherlands). The primary focus is on land use prediction/simulation, especially residential construction, as a major driver of land use change. The study uses multiple future scenarios (Divided Europe, European Coordination, Global Competition) with quantitative spatial modeling producing mapped LULC projections for 2020. The model integrates multiple land use categories and applies regional constraints and suitability maps, producing spatially explicit land use allocations. Environmental impacts are assessed based on these quantitative LULC predictions. Although explicit quantitative accuracy metrics (e.g., accuracy percentages) are not detailed, the paper includes quantitative analyses of land use changes and scenario comparisons with spatial outputs. The scale is national, the focus is on LULC prediction, multiple scenarios are used, and spatially explicit mapped outputs are presented. Therefore, it meets the core inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.)
